memory_update.text: CHEF should remain in the restaurant distribution/procurement universe as a mid-cap specialty distributor with direct independent-restaurant, chef, specialty-SKU, and protein exposure.

WEST should remain as an underfollowed second-order candidate tied to B2B coffee, tea, extracts, ingredients, roasting, packaging, and distribution for foodservice and restaurant channels; needs financial-quality verification.

HFFG is a speculative shadow candidate because of sub-USD-300M market cap, but it has direct niche foodservice-distribution exposure to Asian restaurants, cold chain, seafood, specialty imports, produce, and packaging.

For restaurant themes, owned or controlled procurement and distribution can be an underappreciated profit and franchise-economics lever; Domino's supply-chain structure is a useful context anchor even though DPZ is not an underfollowed discovery candidate.

Layer 2 should verify gross-margin pass-through, route density, working-capital strain, food inflation sensitivity, customer concentration, supplier concentration, and whether specialty distributors have pricing power or merely commodity volume exposure.

node: Foodservice distribution, procurement scale, cold chain, and specialty input sourcing
summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around foodservice distribution and procurement. The reference lane uses a larger distributor to benchmark route density, distribution-center scale, and broadline restaurant exposure. The underfollowed lane emphasizes specialty distributors and B2B beverage/input suppliers that can be hidden inside staples, logistics, or private-label labels rather than restaurant equities. The strongest underfollowed candidates from this pass are CHEF and WEST; HFFG and FARM are more speculative because of sub-USD-300M market cap and/or financial-quality risk, but they have unusually direct node relevance.
